title: Continuous tiling scheduler with attention sparsity prober for prefill/decode
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Problem: current prefill/decode splitters create fixed microphases which sometimes mismatch kernel-native tiling sizes and miss opportunities where attention matrices are sparse. That leads to suboptimal kernel selection (memory-bound kernels used where compute-bound variants would be faster) and either wasted cycles or latency spikes under mixed workloads. Goal: design and implement a continuous tiling scheduler that probes attention sparsity early in the prefill stage and produces dynamically-sized tiles aligned to kernels' sweet spots, while enforcing fairness and latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler integrates with kernel-selection API and returns tile->kernel mappings for each request in prod simulation
End-to-end p50 latency for baseline mixed workload improves by >=6% and p95 does not regress more than 3% compared to current stable
Per-token GPU utilization increases for long-prefill-heavy workloads by >=8% without increasing cost per token by >2%
Automated canary rollout with traffic % gating and rollback if error-rate or latency regression detected
technical_notes: Probe step: lightweight attention-sparsity estimator runs on the first prefill block (prefix). It uses a quantized sampled attention pass (approximate top-k density estimate) to classify request as dense/mid/sparse within 200us median overhead.

Continuous tiling: instead of fixed microphase sizes, scheduler produces tiles of variable length chosen to align with kernel tile sizes (e.g., 64/128/256) and memory footprint targets, constrained by remaining latency budget.

Kernel hints: scheduler consults kernel-performance table (latency/cost per tile size per model family) and emits a kernel_hint for the runtime router. If probe uncertainty > threshold, scheduler hedges by creating one fast low-precision tile path and one high-precision fallback path to avoid latency cliffs.

Fairness policy: token-phase budgets are throttled by per-customer short-term SLA tokens; when contention occurs we degrade throughput-friendly tiles first, preserving low-latency tiles for high-priority customers.
Fallbacks: if attention probe fails or conflicts with routing constraints (dedicated vs hosted limits), scheduler falls back to current stable phase-splitter to guarantee safety.

Metrics: add tile-level metrics (tile_size, kernel_hint, probe_result, probe_latency, chosen_kernel, tile_sched_latency) and per-request lineage to trace tiles in Console. These feed Optimize to refine kernel-performance table.
Performance testing: use recorded traffic (sanitized) from production traces and the runtime perf harness; run A/B with 200k requests to estimate p50/p95 and GPU util curves.
tasks: Implement sparse-probe lightweight pass and add unit tests
Integrate tiling decision into scheduler and emit kernel_hint
Add fairness throttler hook that consults per-tenant short-term budgets
Expose tile-level metrics in runtime and wire to Console
Run perf A/B with production traces and iterate kernel-performance table
Prepare canary rollout plan and alert/rollback rules
